Mickey Rottner was an American professional basketball player.
Marvin "Mickey" Rottner was born on March 23, 1919.
Mickey Rottner played three seasons of professional basketball before the formation of the National Basketball Association.
Mickey Rottner attended Tuley High School in Chicago.
Mickey Rottner played collegiately at Loyola University in Chicago.
Mickey Rottner played for the Ramblers at Loyola University from 1939 to 1942.
Mickey Rottner was named to Loyola University's athletics hall of fame.
Mickey Rottner played professionally after his college career.
Mickey Rottner played in the National Basketball League (NBL) for the Sheboygan Red Skins from 1945 to 1946.
Mickey Rottner averaged four points per game for the Sheboygan Red Skins.
The Sheboygan Red Skins made it to the NBL finals.
The Sheboygan Red Skins lost to the Rochester Royals in the NBL finals.
Mickey Rottner moved to the Basketball Association of America (BAA).
Mickey Rottner played for the Chicago Stags in the BAA.
Mickey Rottner played for the Chicago Stags for two seasons.
Mickey Rottner averaged 5.4 points per game for the Chicago Stags.
Mickey Rottner averaged 1.4 assists per game for the Chicago Stags.
